products.title: Round Platter
products.subtitle: Limoges Porcelain with Pink and 24-Carat Gold Champs de Tulipes Motif

paragraphs: The round platter is unveiled as part of the Champs de Tulipes collection, paying tribute to the Tulipe line designed by Mr. Dior and to the delicate tulip flower, a symbol of love and renewal. Crafted in Limoges porcelain, the platter is elevated by 24-carat gold and features graceful pink petals for a beautifully poetic effect. The creation will lend a luminous touch to tables and can be coordinated with other pieces from the collection to compose a floral ode to the art of living and hosting. Creation by Alexia Lignon for Dior

products.title: Set of Two Cereal Bowls
products.subtitle: White Ceramic with Raised Lily Dior Motif

paragraphs: The set of two cereal bowls is unveiled as part of Cordelia de Castellane's Lily Dior collection. Paying tribute to the lily of the valley, Mr. Dior's favorite flower and eternal lucky charm, the set is crafted in white ceramic embellished with lilies of the valley in a subtle raised pattern. The design will lend a delicate touch to tables and can be coordinated with other creations from the Lily Dior collection for a resolutely poetic atmosphere.
bullets: White Ceramic with Raised Lily Dior Motif

paragraphs: The dinner plate is unveiled as part of Cordelia de Castellane's Les Gris-Gris de Monsieur Dior collection and is embellished with the clover, Christian Dior's treasured symbol and lucky charm. Crafted in ecru ceramic elevated by delicate colors, it celebrates the art of living and the founding couturier's passion for superstition. The design will enhance tables with the House's iconic codes and can be coordinated with other creations from the collection for a poetic and joyous atmosphere.

A small, bustling beehive, that's what my house was when I presented my first collection, wrote Christian Dior in his memoir. This metaphor for the atelier at 30 Avenue Montaigne evokes the gestures of the seamstresses, conscientious and busy like a passionate and masterful swarm. Today, this majestic insect finds its place in the heart of a bucolic collection designed by Cordelia de Castellane, the Creative Director of Maison Dior, composed of earthenware plates that play with soft honey hues.

On the occasion of the opening of the Monsieur Dior restaurant at 30 Avenue Montaigne, Dior Maison is unveiling an exclusive version of the self-titled collection, Monsieur Dior, designed specifically for this unique location. Punctuated by delicate black and white stripes, the collection – which includes plates, bowls, salad bowls and tea and coffee services – is now embellished with the captivating designs of Italian artist Pietro Ruffo. The precious gold-finish ornaments are enhanced by a flourish of arabesques, like an angel or the House's hallmark lucky star. An exceptional collection that embodies the couture spirit and art de vivre so dear to Mr. Dior.
